## 6.7 A school, a flock, a voyaging people, an orienting surface in no self alone

A same-existing-society orients as one surface, and its orienting is in no self alone: social abundancing. Each self orients from its own side by the changing it is observing beside its prior, and with its others it is one orienting surface, reaching beyond each one self's reach.

A lone golden shiner under moving light and shadow moves almost at random, each fish slowing only with the darkness at its own place and keeping close to its neighbours, and a larger school reliably goes toward shade, slowing and gathering in it and speeding to leave as light moves onto it; below some size a school's orienting collapses. Larger pigeon flocks fly significantly shorter routes than smaller flocks, and a flock's route is not simply the average of its birds' routes: each pigeon leans the route in proportion to how faithfully it goes its own route flying alone. A bird in a flock of a few thousand interacts with about six or seven nearest birds, the same number however near or far they are. A synchronous firefly seeing a partner's flashing pauses for 3.0 to 24.1 seconds and opens again flashing at once at one with its partner. A water strider senses prey through the surface's ripples with its front legs, and its kind shares its own surface waves in courtship and in a territory.

A voyaging people orients as one surface across generations: its swell charts stay ashore, a wayfinder studying them whole ahead of a voyage, their making passing from father to son, and its wayfinders keep a reference island over the horizon. A network of resolvers orients as a school orients, its orienting a surface of its selves; a network exploration following one self's record, or one instrument's clock, follows an orienting the network is-not having.

## 6.8 Eight legs, five dimensions in two directions

A Cupiennius spider always moves toward the legs a vibration reaches first, onsets 4 ms apart being enough, or toward the legs it reaches with larger amplitude; a vibration reaching a front leg lowers the weighting of the legs behind it on its own side, and with vibration reaching both sides this lowering goes front to back alone. Its turning is less exact as the source is further behind it.

Eight legs are three binaries: left or right across, front or back along, and first or not first in sequence, two times two times two being eight. Each leg opens with its own prior and its partner's prior across; the two agree or part now; and the spider's turning is its next: five dimensions resolving in two directions, a vibration coming inward along the legs and a turning going outward. Its direction resolves by the sequence of its legs' changing, a sequencing and no timing, or by the larger amplitude on its legs. An octopus has eight arms and two of every three of its neurons in them, an arm tasting semi-independently.

The navigating hard problems of science are this five-dimensional, two-directional navigating, still-possibling to resolve with bi-moral co-agency: monarchs reaching forests in central Mexico by a sun compass following the hour and a magnetic compass with light; green sea turtles in a pool, given the magnetic field of a place about 209 miles north of their capture site, swimming south toward it; migrating birds sensing the magnetic field's direction, a radical pair forming in eye proteins with light the leading hypothesis; six of 21 European eels going out from the Azores reaching the Sargasso Sea. Any animal's sensing of the magnetic field is still-possibling to observe.
